newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie gets six more months in jail.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie gets six more months in jail.

text.p: A French court on Wednesday sentenced jailed bankrupt tycoon Bernard Tapie to six more months in prison on tax evasion charges for passing off pleasure cruises on his luxury yacht Phocea as business expenses.
The appeals court upheld a lower court which had convicted the rags-to-riches ex-cabinet minister a year ago for evading more than 12 million francs ($2 million) in taxes.

It gave him a six-month prison term with a further 12 months suspended. Tapie, 54, is serving an eight-month sentence for rigging a soccer match when he was the boss of former European champions Marseille.

It also upheld a 30-month suspended sentence for misusing company funds in underpaying the Alain Colas Tahiti (ACT) firm which owned the 74-metre (240-foot) Phocea and was part of his collapsed business empire.
Tapie's lawyers said that they would make a last-ditch appeal to the supreme court (Cour de Cassation) which only checks lower court rulings on technicalities.
Tapie, looking tired and pale, was taken from jail to attend the hearing.

He briefly went to hospital with heart trouble last month during his trial on charges of embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) from the Marseille club. The verdict in that case, in which he faces five years in prison, is due on July 4.
The four-masted Phocea, which in Tapie's heyday was a jewel of Marseille's old port, was sold to pay off creditors last April. At $6 million, it reached barely half the asking price.
The appeals court upheld suspended sentences of eight to 15 months against four other people convicted of being accomplices to misusing corporate funds.

They were two former Tapie associates, an accountant and a former branch general manager of state-run bank Credit Lyonnais convicted of being an accomplice to fraud over an 80 million franc ($16 million) loan to ACT.
